investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T06:00–06:07Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 129–144 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the agent pod never started, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two eligible nodes have no remaining peer-pod VM quota, and preemption cannot free any slots because no lower-priority victims exist. The agent pod therefore never reaches a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a schedulable agent, and all four required evidence fields remain absent.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or peer-pod VMs are consuming all available slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch has reduced the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes: if the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, fewer nodes are eligible, making exhaustion more likely even at moderate load.
TERTIARY — a prior eval run or leaked agent pod from a previous withCleanup cycle is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up, reducing available capacity by at least one slot.
QUATERNARY — the cluster has not scaled out (no new kata-capable nodes added) to meet demand, and the current 2-node eligible pool is undersized for concurrent probe traffic plus production load.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place any new remote-agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written and the expected-output contract was violated in full.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval runner (and by extension any real remote-agent creation attempt) is stuck Unschedulable. The eval failure is a direct consequence of this infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion: the runner cannot create an agent, so it never reaches the state-polling step and produces no evidence. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-02T06:00–06:07Z because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler: 2 of 6 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No preemption path was available, leaving pods unscheduled for 129–144 seconds until the eval timeout was reached. Because the agent pod never started, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced and the expected-output contract was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two eligible nodes have no remaining peer-pod VM quota, and preemption cannot free any slots because no lower-priority victims exist. The agent pod therefore never reaches a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a schedulable agent, and all four required evidence fields remain absent.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or peer-pod VMs are consuming all available slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch has reduced the schedulable node pool to only 2 nodes: if the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, fewer nodes are eligible, making exhaustion more likely even at moderate load.
TERTIARY — a prior eval run or leaked agent pod from a previous withCleanup cycle is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not cleaned up, reducing available capacity by at least one slot.
QUATERNARY — the cluster has not scaled out (no new kata-capable nodes added) to meet demand, and the current 2-node eligible pool is undersized for concurrent probe traffic plus production load.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Insufficient Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-02 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching pod affinity/selector. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, causing a total contract gap (all 5 required evidence fields — orgId, agentId, model, provider, message — are missing).
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource capacity on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity or selector constraints at all. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for the full timeout duration (~129–150 seconds), preventing agent creation and all downstream eval steps. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a user-facing product outage confirmed by traffic signals.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots on the kata-peerpods node pool are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption is also unavailable, meaning no lower-priority pods can be evicted to make room.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: the 4 nodes that do not match the pod's affinity/selector may represent a node pool that was scaled down, had labels changed, or had taints added, reducing the effective schedulable pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes.

Tertiary — concurrent eval or workload surge: multiple simultaneous remote-agent eval runs or production workloads may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes before this eval's pods could be scheduled.

Lower confidence — node pool health degradation: one or both of the 2 affinity-matching nodes may be in a degraded or cordoned state, further reducing effective VM slot availability even if the resource count appears non-zero at the cluster level.
